subject: Materials Science
title: Stem Cells and Biomaterials
description: A quick, practical guide to Stem Cells and Biomaterials.

hook.text: Mesenchymal stem cells become bone on stiff surfaces, fat on soft ones — the material tells cells what to become.

buildup.text: Substrate stiffness, topography, and chemistry influence stem cell fate — physical cues rival chemical ones.

discovery.text: Nanotopography mimicking collagen fibers guides stem cells without any growth factors — pure mechanical signaling.

twist.text: Cells sense stiffness through mechanotransduction — pulling on the surface and reading the resistance through integrins.

climax.text: Engineered scaffolds now direct stem cells into cartilage, nerve, or liver tissue — all through material properties.

punchline.text: The material whispers to the cell — and the cell becomes what it's told.

quiz.question: How does substrate stiffness influence stem cell fate?
options: Stiffer surfaces always kill stem cells
Cells sense resistance through mechanotransduction and differentiate accordingly
Stiffness has no effect on cell behavior
